description:
NOT save compatible with versions of ArmaA prior to v3.2.6

Support me on Ko-Fi | Changelog

About
A story and content mod primarily focused around pilotable strikecraft: fighter-scale ships with own unique mechanics, over 30 pilotable units across 18 chassis families, 7 warships and carriers built to support them, and 9 fighter wings, a fully fleshed out companion officer, a minor faction with campaign layer elements, and a story centering around a system level conflict centuries in the making.

Can be added mid-save, but best installed on a new save for the full experience. Not all updates are save-compatible; check the changelog.

The mod requires LazyLib and MagicLib.

Recommended:
Nexerelin <-- required for custom start
PAGSM
Caymon's Ship Pack
Sunrider
LunaLib
Knights of Ludd
Project MISTRAL

In the mod, "Strikecraft" refers to a special type of ship that relies on larger ships for travel between systems, crew storage, and maintenance. Most of these can be found in the Gamlin system to the southwest of the core, but some have been added to vanilla factions where appropriate and at halved rates.

Features
- High speed units with good maneuverability and offensive power, but low to mid defensive stats
- Possesses a configurable "repair pool" that can be used to repair and rearm at most ships/carriers with launch bays during combat
- Can fly over ships and other obstacles, but receive up to 25% more damage vs certain weapons and units possessing anti-fighter skills
- Defeat is not the end; for more expendable strikecraft, spare chassis will be deployed upon their destruction

The Gamlin system is home to the Arma Armatura corporation and the people caught in its orbit; among them Dawn Given-To-God, a recruitable officer with her own beliefs, motives, and opinions on the technologies, locales, and factions of the Sector.

Features
- A small star system on the fringes of Luddic space
- A custom start with extra narrative content
- A companion officer who reacts to where you go, what you fly, and who you deal with.
- A pirate mini-faction that attempts to sow anarchy and chaos throughout the Sector.
- Five quests with four uniquely scripted setpiece battles, in locales ranging from high orbit to a city's skies to [REDACTED].
- Cross-mod content with PAGSM and Sunrider
- Alternate and optional 90's RPGesque portrait pack for the anime-inclined

WINGCOM is an unlockable hullmod that crews your carrier's wings with chatty named pilots. They gain experience over the campaign, learn skills as they level, and a rare few have the latent talent to become Ace Pilots.

Features
- Persistent named pilots with personalities, progression, and skills.
- Radio chatter in combat: pilots banter with each other and taunt the enemies they're facing.
- Fully customizable squadrons via the Squadron Management intel screen: names, portraits, callsigns.
- Veteran pilots can be promoted into fully-fledged Officers.

Units that can provide Strikecraft with extended operational time, additional weapons and protection, and the ability to travel independently without need for a carrier. You can freely switch units in and out of these platforms at your colonies so long as you have the appropriate unit.

Credits
maritumix - Campaign Music, Battle Music
BONESAW - Battle Music
+TEK - Music
HzDev, Mycophobia, Zeta04, zaz168 - CN Translation
MesoTroniK - Consult, some SFX
Tartiflette - Initial mech script
Harupea - Initial Docking System
Nia Tahl - Scripting, trail patterns, notWhiteBase
Dark.Revenant - Scripting
Selkie - Some sprites
Caymon Joestar - Some sprites
Quacken - Rajanya's binders, some portraits
Lukas04 - I may have copied his forum post format  ;)
Avanitia,Bass, Alex_Sans, WMGreymind, Randall, Phantasia, Karleen, Finn, Unit9461, TheSoldier, Caymon Joestar, Selkie - Feedback / Testing

The optional anime-style portraits in this mod were generated with DALL·E 3 and edited by hand. Optional voice lines use modified output from ElevenLabs. The illustrations for Jenius and New Meshan were generated with ElevenLabs and edited by hand. LLMs were used for grammar, and syntax passes on written text, and code assistance.
All sprites, and all portraits credited to individual artists are original human work.
